extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, marketers, and press release writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting effective subheadlines (subheads) that sit between a press release headline and body, intended to summarize, entice, and improve discoverability of a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subhead definition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The subheadline (subhead) is a short summary between the press release headline and body text that provides additional context or information about the news of the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public relations professionals use it to highlight key details, emphasize the newsworthiness of the press release, or give a brief overview of the announcement. No matter the route taken, the press release subhead is meant to grab reader attention and encourage them to read on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support the headline
rubrics_metrics.description: The subheadline supports the press release headline with more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subhead can clarify and also entice the reader with further details, adding specificity that complements the headline's promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the subhead as a teaser
rubrics_metrics.description: The subhead can work with the headline as a teaser, to get people to read on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When headlines and subheads are visible when shared, they together increase the chance of capturing journalist attention. Treat the subhead as an enticement that encourages engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search engine visibility (SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subheads can appear in search engine results pages; some search engines will use your subhead to populate the snippet under the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Google often generates its own text, other search engines may use your subhead. Use the subhead to improve discoverability in search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as a concise summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Your subhead can be a useful summary of what your press release is all about, while leaving enough intrigue for readers to read the full release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance summary and intrigue: provide key information but stop short of giving everything away so journalists want to read the entire release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: You should include keywords in your headline and subhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords can relate to your company, brand, niche, or industry and will help journalists and other interested readers find your content via search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use emotive language
rubrics_metrics.description: The best subheadlines can make an emotional connection with the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words with stronger emotional or dramatic impact (e.g., 'slash' vs. 'decrease', 'soar' vs. 'increase') to create a more compelling subhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase brand recognition (use company name)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your company name in your headline and/or subhead to increase brand recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases are an authoritative and trust-building vehicle; including the company name helps build brand awareness since people are less likely to buy from brands they don't trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it brief (aim ~25 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make every word count and aim for around 25 words in your subheadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise: a short, focused subhead is more likely to be read and used by journalists and search engines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the subheadline last
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the subheadline after drafting the rest of the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saving the subhead until last helps you effectively communicate your message because the subhead adds details to clarify the headline and summarize the press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear and intrigue the press and public
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear while trying to intrigue both the press and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The headline is a promise of what readers will learn; the subhead should act as an even stronger tease and enticement to get them to read on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the distribution interface subhead field
rubrics_metrics.description: Most press release distribution service interfaces include a subheadline field you can populate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate this field to take advantage of additional visibility and to provide extra context when the release is distributed or shared.
